title: Configuration and security: Settings (ISiteProperty), application roles (ODC IAppRole / O11 IRole) and screen restriction; client variables are front A's data.client-variable

capabilities.title: Settings (site properties) and application roles
capabilities.summary: ISiteProperty (the ODC product calls it Setting; expressions read Settings.<Name> on ODC, Site.<Name> on O11) with DataType, DefaultValue, Description and, on ODC, IsSecret; an application role created with `create IRole` (ODC answers an IAppRole, O11 an IRole) with Description; a screen restricted with `link from <screen> connector Roles to <role>`.

route.operation: create ISiteProperty|IRole @espace; set DataType/DefaultValue/Description/IsSecret; link {from:<screen>, connector:"Roles", to:<role>}; deliver with studio_deliver / o11_deliver (they validate and refuse before any change)

capabilities.guidance: Addressing outside the creating job: ISiteProperty:<Name>; the ODC role answers as IAppRole. Settings are read-only inside actions on ODC per the security-settings description, but NAO-DA records that write as NOT MEASURED: do not rely on either claim without a proof. IsSecret protects nothing in the model: the flag is independent of the value, DefaultValue stays readable in clear, and the secret value belongs in the Portal (environment configuration). Per-user state on the device, which on ODC also replaces session variables, is front A's data.client-variable; user exceptions are front A's logic.exception.

limits.text: IsSecret protects nothing in the model: the flag is independent of the value, the DefaultValue is written and read back in clear, and the secret lives in the Portal configuration.

differences.text: ODC `create IRole` answers an IAppRole (IRole is only a base interface); O11 answers an IRole.

Expression prefix Settings.<Name> (ODC) vs Site.<Name> (O11); on O11 expressions read Site.<Name> in valid jobs (tickets-02-helpers, tickets-04-collab, tickets-06-sla), while usages of a site property is not proven.
